items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: So he appointed me to committees.

ctx.x: Our merger. Yeah we merged. Now I drifted once again. I first started out talking about the black local and I told you the story about the merger, and then I joined in ’37 in a Subsidiary. Well as I think I mentioned before, in ’45 or around the mid-forties, Petrillo abolished the subsidiary locals. Because you had Subsidiary locals all throughout the United States. You had also black chartered locals and they had charters that went back to the early 1900’s and some even the late 1800’s in Chicago, 10-208, so I…

subsidiaries as full members. Parent local they called it, or failing that, why that’s how we came to have the charter of 669. So in 669 we set up, had our offices, we had a President, we had the Secretary/Treasurer/Business Agent and we had another office secretary and we had a Board of Directors. And I was on the Board of Directors. I got elected to the Board of Directors. And so we asked them on numerous occasions about amalgamation merger. Even one time we got it on the ballot through white friends. But it…
